name: Api Design Best Practices
description: This module captures the best practices for api design, distilled from common failure modes and what tends to hold up over time.
content:
This module captures the best practices for api design, distilled from common failure modes and what tends to hold up over time.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Measure before optimizing any api design bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
2. When api design guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
3. When multiple api design strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
4. Check that api design terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
5. When api design decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
6. Re-check edge cases relevant to api design (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
7. Before starting api design work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
8. State assumptions about api design explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
9. Surface known limitations of a chosen api design approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
10. Prefer explicit, readable api design solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid introducing new api design abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not silently drop api design edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of api design correctness.
- Avoid mixing unrelated api design concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for api design, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
